commitResults.messageTitle: Rename chatbot from Duke to XiaoZhi
Changed echo into storing list of tasks
Added marking function and create new Task class
Added different task classes, and added tests
Added exception handling and edited tests accordingly
Changed to use enums instead of if else
Add automatic task save/load to disk
commitResults.messageBody:
Tasks created in a session live only in memory, so all of them are
lost the moment XiaoZhi exits.

A user cannot reopen the app and continue from where they left off,
and anyone running the project for the first time has no save file
to load from, since ./data doesn't exist on a fresh machine.

Let's,
* add a Storage class that owns all file reading/writing
* give each Task subclass a toSaveFormat()/getTypeIcon() pair
  mirroring its existing toString() override, so encoding stays
  polymorphic instead of adding type-checks in Storage
* create the data folder automatically when saving, and treat a
  missing save file as an empty list when loading
* skip corrupted lines with a warning instead of crashing on load
* ignore /data/ in git, since it holds generated user data

Tasks are saved right after each command completes successfully,
rather than only on exit, so a crash or force-quit mid-session does
not lose earlier progress.

Deadline and Event store their /by, /from and /to values as plain
Strings, so XiaoZhi treats a date exactly like any other free-text
description.

This means users can type anything after /by (typos, forgotten
dates), there's no consistent display format, and any later feature
that needs to reason about a task's actual date (e.g., listing what's
due on a given day) has nothing to work with.

Let's,
* add a Dates helper that parses yyyy-mm-dd input into a LocalDate,
  raising a XiaoZhiException with a clear message on anything else
* change Deadline.by and Event.from/to from String to LocalDate
* display dates as MMM dd yyyy (e.g. Dec 02 2019) in toString(),
  while keeping the on-disk save format as the same yyyy-mm-dd text,
  since LocalDate's own toString() already matches it exactly
* update Storage.parseTask() to parse dates the same way when
  loading from disk
* update ui-test-plan.md: existing deadline/event tests now use real
  yyyy-mm-dd input and check the new display format, and two new
  tests cover the invalid-date error message

Using the same yyyy-mm-dd text for both user input and the save file
means no separate on-disk date format is needed - LocalDate.parse()
and LocalDate.toString() are already inverses of each other.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Ui to own all console input/output
commitResults.messageBody:
XiaoZhi.java mixes three concerns in one file: parsing commands,
mutating the task list, and printing to/reading from the console.
The banner, greeting, farewell, and per-command messages are all
System.out.println calls scattered through store()'s switch, plus a
Scanner XiaoZhi owns directly.

This makes XiaoZhi hard to read (business logic is interleaved with
formatting strings) and blocks the next extractions the target asks
for: Parser and TaskList shouldn't need to know how a message is
worded or where input comes from, only Ui should.

Let's,
* add a Ui class owning the Scanner and every showX()/readCommand()
  method: showBanner, showGreeting, showFarewell, showAdded,
  showRemoved, showMarked, showUnmarked, showList, showError
* replace XiaoZhi's five static print helpers and its inline
  System.out.println calls with calls to a single Ui instance,
  passed into store() as a parameter
* drop the Scanner field and java.util.Scanner import from
  XiaoZhi.java, since Ui now owns the only Scanner

This is a pure extraction: every message's wording, punctuation and
call site stays byte-for-byte identical, so the full 19-case UI test
suite (test/run_ui_tests.py) passes unchanged with no test-plan
updates needed. store() still takes a Ui parameter rather than
XiaoZhi becoming an instance class with a ui field - that reshape is
better done together with the TaskList/Parser extractions, once
there's more than one field to justify it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract Parser and Command hierarchy; reshape XiaoZhi around them
commitResults.messageBody:
XiaoZhi.store() was still doing three jobs at once: deciding what a
command means, checking it's valid, and (via inline code, then via a
switch that built Command objects) carrying it out. The switch itself,
and the enum that drives it, still lived inside XiaoZhi - exactly what
the target's Parser class is meant to own.

Let's,
* add a Parser class with a single static parse(String) -> Command,
  moving the whole CommandWord enum and switch expression out of
  XiaoZhi verbatim
* add an abstract Command with execute(TaskList, Ui, Storage) and a
  default isExit() -> false, plus ListCommand, MarkCommand,
  UnmarkCommand, DeleteCommand, ExitCommand, and one AddCommand(Task)
  that replaces the three near-identical TODO/DEADLINE/EVENT branches
* move each MARK/UNMARK/DELETE command's "does this index exist"
  bounds-check out of the switch (now Parser) and into that command's
  own execute() - Parser.parse(String) only ever receives the raw
  input text, not the TaskList it would need to check against, while
  execute() already receives one, so that's naturally where the check
  belongs now
* move storage.save(...) out of the loop's common tail into each
  mutating command's own execute(), since ListCommand and ExitCommand
  never needed it
* replace XiaoZhi's static main()+store(Ui) pair with an instance: a
  constructor that builds ui, storage and tasks once, and a run() that
  owns the read-parse-execute loop
* finish wiring TaskList through Ui.showList(...), started but not yet
  committed in the previous step
* rename the enum from Command to CommandWord (it now lives in Parser)
  so the name Command is free for the new abstract class

This finishes both the minimal target (Ui, Storage, Parser, TaskList
each own their piece) and the stretch goal (the Command hierarchy),
with XiaoZhi.run() now reading close to the target's own skeleton:
parse, execute, check isExit. All 19 UI test cases still pass
unmodified - every error message, its wording, and the order
validation happens in is unchanged, just relocated to whichever class
now owns that responsibility.

commitResults.messageTitle: Divide classes into packages by responsibility
commitResults.messageBody:
All 18 classes lived flat in src/main/java, with no grouping to show
which ones belong together. That's fine for a handful of files, but
makes it harder to see the program's shape at a glance as the class
count grows - task types are then indistinguishable from commands or
plumbing just by looking at the file listing.

Let's,
* create a xiaozhi package (kept as the source root's only top-level
  package, containing just XiaoZhi.java, the entry point) and seven
  sub-packages: xiaozhi.command (Command and its seven subclasses),
  xiaozhi.task (Task, Todo, Deadline, Event, TaskList),
  xiaozhi.parser (Parser), xiaozhi.storage (Storage), xiaozhi.ui (Ui),
  xiaozhi.exception (XiaoZhiException), and xiaozhi.util (Dates)
* git mv each file into its new package folder, add the matching
  package declaration, and add whatever imports it now needs to reach
  classes outside its own package
* update test/run_ui_tests.py's compile step to glob **/*.java instead
  of *.java (it only searched the top-level source dir before), and
  its run step to invoke xiaozhi.XiaoZhi instead of the now-invalid
  bare XiaoZhi

src/main/java stays the source root - nothing above the xiaozhi
package is touched, matching what the exercise asks for. Grouping is
by responsibility (task/command/parser/storage/ui) rather than one
flat xiaozhi package, since the class count here already justifies it
per the stretch goal. This is a pure move: no method bodies changed,
so all 19 UI test cases still pass unmodified.

The Gradle support merged in from add-gradle-support was written for
the original seedu.duke.Duke template - its application block and
shadowJar output name still referred to that class and jar name,
neither of which exist in this project after the MoreOOP and Packages
increments.

Let's,
* set application.mainClass to xiaozhi.XiaoZhi, matching the actual
  entry point after the A-Packages restructuring
* rename the shadowJar output from duke.jar to xiaozhi.jar to match

No other part of the provided build.gradle was touched.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests for Dates and Storage
commitResults.messageBody:
The project has no automated tests yet beyond the manual UI test
script - every change so far has been verified by hand-running
test/run_ui_tests.py, which only exercises the program end-to-end
through its console I/O and can't isolate which class actually broke.

Let's,
* add DatesTest, covering Dates.parse()'s happy path, whitespace
  trimming, rejecting non-date text with the expected guidance
  message, rejecting a calendar date that doesn't exist (Feb 30) even
  though it's textually well-formed, and Dates.format()'s padding
* add StorageTest, covering a save-then-load round trip across all
  three task types (including a marked-done flag), a missing save
  file returning an empty list instead of erroring, one corrupted
  line among valid ones being skipped without losing the others, and
  the parent folder being created automatically on first save

Dates and Storage were picked because they're pure enough to test
without mocking (no console I/O to capture, and Storage's only side
effect - the filesystem - is isolated per test via JUnit's @TempDir),
while still each having real branching logic worth catching
regressions in. Parser and the Command classes are more involved to
test cleanly (Parser returns opaque Command objects, and Command
subclasses read Ui/Storage as collaborators) and are left for a later
pass toward the stretch goal of covering every non-trivial method.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Javadoc to all public classes and non-trivial methods
commitResults.messageBody:
Every public class, constructor and non-trivial method across the 17
touched files now has a proper header comment: a short verb-led summary
sentence plus @param/@return/@throws where relevant. Getters/setters
and unmodified @Override methods are left undocumented per the coding
standard's own exemption. Storage.java was already fully documented
and needed no change.

No behaviour change — javac -Xlint:all, the UI test suite (19/19) and
the JUnit suite (11/11) all pass exactly as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix coding-standard layout violations: ternaries and switch-case indent
commitResults.messageBody:
Audited the codebase against the SE-EDU intermediate Java coding
standard. Two real violations, both indentation-depth issues:

- Parser.parse()'s TODO/DEADLINE/EVENT ternaries combined
  "? consequent : alternative" onto one continuation line instead of
  the standard's 3-line form (condition / ? consequent / : alternative,
  each wrapped line +8 spaces from the parent).
- Every case label in both switch expressions (Parser.parse(),
  Storage.parseTask()) sat at the same indentation as the switch
  keyword itself instead of one level (+4 spaces) deeper, as the
  standard's own switch example shows.

Layout only, no behaviour change — javac -Xlint:all, the UI test
suite (19/19) and the JUnit suite (11/11) all pass exactly as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add find command to search tasks by keyword
commitResults.messageBody:
A new "find <keyword>" command searches every task's description for a
case-insensitive substring match and lists the matches, numbered from
1, in their original list order. Follows the existing command shape:
Parser builds a FindCommand from the keyword, TaskList.find() does the
actual search (via a new Task.getDescription() accessor), Ui.showFound()
owns the output formatting. An empty keyword is rejected the same way
an empty todo description already is.

Added 4 new UI test cases (Tests 20-23): matches across all three task
types, no matches, case-insensitivity, and an empty keyword error.

javac -Xlint:all, the UI test suite (23/23) and the JUnit suite (11/11)
all pass.

commitResults.messageTitle: Set up Checkstyle for code style enforcement
commitResults.messageBody:
The project currently has no automated check for the SE-EDU Java
coding standard beyond manual review.

Let's add the checkstyle Gradle plugin along with a checkstyle.xml
and suppressions.xml matching the AddressBook Level 3 reference
config, and fix the one violation it caught (trailing whitespace
in Ui.java's banner text block).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a JavaFX GUI for XiaoZhi
commitResults.messageBody:
XiaoZhi currently only has a console interface, per the CS2103T
JavaFX tutorial parts 1-4.

Let's add a xiaozhi.gui package (Launcher, Main, MainWindow, DialogBox)
that loads MainWindow.fxml/DialogBox.fxml and drives the existing
Parser/Command/TaskList/Storage pipeline through a new
XiaoZhi.getResponse(String) bridge method, instead of duplicating
that logic. getResponse() temporarily redirects System.out to capture
what Ui would otherwise print to the console, since Ui's methods
print directly rather than returning text.

`./gradlew run` now launches the GUI (application.mainClass points
at the new Launcher); XiaoZhi.main() is untouched, so the console
mode still works directly.

The avatar images are simple generated placeholders, since the
tutorial's starter repo ships no art assets.

commitResults.messageTitle: Ui: use varargs to print multi-line output
commitResults.messageBody:
Every method in Ui that shows more than one line (showAdded,
showRemoved, showList, etc.) built it as its own sequence of
System.out.println calls, repeating "one line per call" in six
different places.

Let's pull that into a single private print(String... lines) helper
and have every multi-line method call it instead, either with the
lines spelled out directly (showAdded, showMarked, ...) or, for
showList/showFound where the number of lines is only known at
runtime, with a String[] built by a small numberedLines() helper.
Output is unchanged.

The GUI so far used JavaFX's default look: unstyled chat bubbles, a
plain scroll pane, and no visual feedback on what kind of command a
reply came from.

Let's add main.css (window/input/button/scrollbar theming) and
dialog-box.css (message bubble shapes), linked from MainWindow.fxml
and DialogBox.fxml respectively. DialogBox now also tints its bubble
by the command that produced it, via a getCommandType() added to
XiaoZhi (mirroring getResponse()) that reports the executed command's
simple class name: green for a task added, orange for marked done,
red for deleted, and the plain reply-label look for everything else
(list, find, unmark, exit, and unrecognised input).

commitResults.messageTitle: Add assertions to document internal invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
Several internal methods rely on invariants that are enforced by their
callers rather than checked locally: TaskList.get() and remove() assume
the index was already range-checked by the calling Command, and
Dates.format() assumes it is only ever given a date that came from
Dates.parse().

These assumptions are easy to break silently in future changes, since
violating them would not fail loudly; they would produce wrong output or
an unrelated exception far from the real bug.

Let's add Java assert statements at each of these points to document the
assumption inline and fail fast, with a message explaining what should
always be true and why.

Assertions are used only for conditions that should never be false if
the rest of the code is correct (programmer errors), never for user-
input validation, which continues to throw XiaoZhiException with a user-
facing message as before. Assertions are disabled by default at runtime
and only take effect when the JVM is started with -ea (Gradle already
does this for the `test` task); they exist here to document and catch
programming mistakes during development.

commitResults.messageTitle: Parser: extract command parsing into helpers
commitResults.messageBody:
Parser.parse() is a single ~140-line method handling all ten command
words in one switch expression. The mark, unmark and delete branches
each repeat the same seven lines that split the input and parse a
1-based task number, differing only in the exception message and which
Command subtype they produce.

Per the code quality guidelines (Avoid Long Methods, Single Level of
Abstraction, Minimize Code Duplication), a method this long that mixes
raw string-parsing detail with top-level command dispatch, and
duplicates the same parsing logic three times, is hard to read and risks
the three copies drifting apart if one is ever fixed without the others.

Let's extract each command word's parsing logic into its own private
helper method (parseTaskIndex, parseFindKeyword, parseTodo,
parseDeadline, parseEvent), with mark/unmark/delete sharing one
parseTaskIndex(fullCommand, action) helper. parse() itself now just
identifies the command word and dispatches to the matching helper, all
at the same level of abstraction.

This keeps every error message and parsing rule byte-for-byte identical
to before - verified by running
todo/deadline/event/find/mark/unmark/delete/list/bye, plus the out-of-
range and unknown-command error paths, through the parser with
assertions enabled; output matched the pre-refactor behaviour exactly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01EZoRkUMoGvgq4LhwdY6vCj
Parser: extract command parsing into helpers

`./gradlew checkstyleMain` has not actually been run against the GUI
code since it was added: Checkstyle was set up before the JavaFX GUI
existed, and nobody re-ran it against xiaozhi.gui afterwards, so these
violations sat unnoticed.

The CI workflow just added on this branch runs `./gradlew check` on
every push, so it caught them immediately and failed every job, blocking
this very PR from going green.

Let's fix the two violations Checkstyle actually flagged. DialogBox's
switch-case block had its case labels flush against `switch` (no indent)
instead of the 4-space caseIndent checkstyle.xml configures. Main.java
and MainWindow.java each had a blank line between their javafx.* and
xiaozhi.* imports, even though CustomImportOrder groups both under the
same THIRD_PARTY_PACKAGE bucket, which needs no separator inside a
single group.

No behaviour changes here, purely whitespace and import ordering.
Confirmed this covers everything Checkstyle flagged: the failing run
reported exactly 13 errors across 3 files, matching DialogBox.java (11)
+ Main.java (1) + MainWindow.java (1).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01EZoRkUMoGvgq4LhwdY6vCj
Set up CI with GitHub Actions

XiaoZhi has no way to reverse a mistake. A typo'd todo, an accidental
delete, or a mis-typed mark/unmark index can only be fixed by manually
re-entering the opposite command, and for a delete that means retyping
the whole task description and losing its original position in the list.

Undo is one of the most basic safety nets a task manager can offer, and
every mutating command here already goes through the same
execute(TaskList, Ui, Storage) shape, making a symmetric reversal a
natural fit.

Let's add an undo command that reverses the most recently executed
undoable command. Command gains an isUndoable()/undo() pair (default:
not undoable, since list/find/exit have nothing to reverse); AddCommand,
DeleteCommand, MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand override both. A new
CommandHistory stack is threaded through execute() alongside
tasks/ui/storage, and XiaoZhi pushes each command onto it right after
execute() returns without error, provided isUndoable() says so.
UndoCommand pops the stack and calls undo() on whatever it finds,
throwing if it's empty.

DeleteCommand's undo reinserts the removed task at its original index
(new TaskList.insert()) rather than the end of the list.
Mark/UnmarkCommand's undo restores the task's exact done-state from
immediately before that command ran, rather than blindly toggling it, so
undoing a repeated mark/unmark (already a no-op) stays a no-op instead
of flipping the status incorrectly.

Threading CommandHistory through execute()'s parameter list, rather than
storing it on TaskList, keeps the task package from having to import
anything from the command package -- only Command and its subclasses
need to know the history exists.

Also gives XiaoZhi's GUI an undo-label bubble tint, matching the
existing per-command-type styling in DialogBox/dialog-box.css.

While adding UI test cases for undo, found and fixed two unrelated pre-
existing issues in the test harness: run_ui_tests.py now runs each test
case in its own temp directory, since every test case sharing one
working directory let an earlier test's saved tasks silently leak into
the next one's task count; and ui-test-plan.md's mark/unmark test case
had a stray trailing space in its expected output that never actually
matched Ui's message text.

commitResults.messageTitle: Redesign GUI with asymmetric aurora theme
commitResults.messageBody:
XiaoZhi's GUI mirrors the user and the bot as identical chat bubbles,
never distinguishes an error reply from a normal one, shows a large
profile picture on every single message, and is locked to a fixed
400x600 window that does not adapt if resized.

The A-BetterGui exercise calls for exactly these kinds of GUI-quality
fixes, and the current look also leaves little room for XiaoZhi's
often multi-line replies.

Let's,
* give the user a compact, right-aligned bubble and XiaoZhi a
  full-width, left-aligned card instead of two mirrored bubbles,
  since this is a conversation with an app, not with another person
* have XiaoZhi report a distinct "Error" command type so failed
  input gets an alarmed red card instead of blending in with a
  normal reply
* drop the large per-message avatar images entirely -- the two
  speakers never change, so a single small avatar in the header is
  enough, and it frees up width for the reply text
* switch the root layout from a fixed AnchorPane to a BorderPane,
  fit the chat area to the window's width, and cap the user's
  bubble width to a fraction of it, so resizing the window reflows
  the content instead of leaving it clipped or stranded
* restyle the window with a translucent "glass" card look over a
  soft purple/blue aurora background

The aurora/glass look was one of several directions mocked up and
picked beforehand. JavaFX has no true background blur, so the
"glass" panels use translucency plus a soft border instead of an
actual blur-through effect.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reskin XiaoZhi as Master Zhi, the wise sage
commitResults.messageBody:
XiaoZhi's replies are plain and generic ("Got it.", "OOPS!!!"), and the
Glass Aurora GUI from A-BetterGui has no distinguishing character behind
its colors.

The A-Personality exercise asks for a unique personality expressed
through the chatbot's name, its phrases, and its GUI, chosen from a set
of directions mocked up and approved beforehand.

Let's give XiaoZhi the persona of Master Zhi: a calm, proverb-speaking
sage.
* rename the on-screen name and window title from XiaoZhi to Master Zhi
  (the Java class/package names are untouched -- this is the persona the
  user sees, not the codebase identity)
* rewrite every line Ui prints -- greeting, farewell, add/delete/mark/
  unmark, the list/find headings, and the error prefix -- into short,
  proverb-like phrasing, plus the "task doesn't exist", "nothing to
  undo" and "unrecognised command" messages raised elsewhere
* re-theme main.css and dialog-box.css from the aurora's purple/blue
  glass look to a dark ink-green ground with gold hairlines and an
  italic serif pairing, keeping every structural win from A-BetterGui
  (asymmetric bubbles, resizable window, the dedicated error card)
  untouched
* recolor the header avatar and send button to a gold ink-drop mark

This keeps the fine-grained Parser validation messages (missing /by,
invalid date, etc.) as plain usage instructions rather than folding them
into the voice, since clarity matters more there than character.

test/ui-test-plan.md's expected output is updated in lockstep with every
phrase change via a scripted, verified find/replace (not retyped by
hand), so its 31 cases still describe the program's real behavior.

This environment has no javac available to actually compile or run
test/run_ui_tests.py, so verification here was manual: line-length,
brace/quote-balance and FXML well-formedness checks, plus a full re-read
of every changed file and diff. Please run `./gradlew build test` and
`python3 test/run_ui_tests.py` before merging.

commitResults.messageTitle: Rename preposition-shaped fields to real nouns
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadline.by and Event.from/to name their date fields after the
prepositions used in the command syntax (/by, /from, /to), and
DialogBox.getXiaoZhiDialog() names its local variable db.

The CS2103T naming guide (W4.6b) asks for nouns naming things and
verbs naming actions; "by", "from" and "to" are prepositions, not
nouns, and "db" is short enough to misread as "database" rather than
"dialog box" (W4.6e: not too short).

Let's rename Deadline.by to byDate, Event.from/to to fromDate/toDate,
and DialogBox's db to dialogBox, updating every reference, the
constructor parameters, and their Javadoc to match.

These fields are only ever read inside their own class (toString(),
toSaveFormat()), so the rename is fully contained to the three files
touched here.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01MpjHywwGZjp7q1uh5aiYSx

commitResults.messageTitle: Add JUnit tests covering nearly all testable code
commitResults.messageBody:
XiaoZhi currently has automated tests only for Storage and Dates;
Task, TaskList, Parser, every Command, CommandHistory, and the
XiaoZhi.getResponse() pipeline that the GUI drives all run
unverified except by hand.

Let's write JUnit tests for everything the A-MoreTesting exercise
says can be tested automatically: Todo/Deadline/Event (via the
shared Task behaviour), TaskList, Parser (every validation branch,
not just the happy path), all 8 Command subclasses including their
undo() contracts, CommandHistory, and end-to-end XiaoZhi.getResponse()
integration tests. GUI classes (xiaozhi.gui.*) are left to manual
testing per the exercise's own guidance, since a JavaFX Application
can't be driven from a headless JUnit run without a test framework
this project doesn't otherwise need.

A small OutputCapture test utility redirects System.out into a
buffer for the duration of a block, so Command tests can assert on
Ui's console-reporting side effects the same way XiaoZhi.getResponse()
already does internally, without pulling in a mocking library. Command
tests use @TempDir with a real Storage, matching the existing
StorageTest pattern, so they also exercise persistence rather than
just in-memory state.

One regression this suite specifically guards against: a command
that parses successfully but fails during execute() (e.g. "mark 5"
on an empty list) must not be pushed onto the undo history, or a
later undo would silently reverse the wrong thing. XiaoZhiTest
covers this directly by issuing a failing command between two
successful ones and checking undo still reverses only the earlier
success.

This sandbox has no javac available, so these tests are written and
statically checked (line length, brace/paren balance, checkstyle's
import grouping) but not compiled or run here -- please run
`./gradlew test` before merging.

Rename preposition-shaped fields to real nouns

commitResults.messageTitle: Fix SeparatorWrap violations in new tests
commitResults.messageBody:
checkstyleTest fails on branch-A-MoreTesting: every assertThrows(...)
and OutputCapture.capture(...) call that wraps its lambda argument
onto a new line put that line's leading "(" -- the lambda's own empty
parameter list -- at the very start of the line, e.g.:

    assertThrows(XiaoZhiException.class,
            () -> Parser.parse("deadline /by 2019-12-02"));

SeparatorWrap's "eol" option for LPAREN requires the opposite: an
opening parenthesis at a line wrap belongs at the end of the previous
line, not the start of the next one, the same way the surrounding
method calls in this codebase already wrap.

Let's move "() ->" up onto the previous line in all 16 places this
pattern occurs, across ParserTest, DeleteCommandTest,
UnmarkCommandTest, UndoCommandTest, AddCommandTest and
MarkCommandTest, so the lambda's body is what continues onto the
wrapped line instead:

    assertThrows(XiaoZhiException.class, () ->
            Parser.parse("deadline /by 2019-12-02"));

Confirmed via `./gradlew build` that checkstyleTest, test and check
all pass now.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commitResults.messageTitle: Pad Stage min size by title-bar chrome to fix bottom-bar clipping
commitResults.messageBody:
Dragging the window small enough leaves the input bar sliced off at
the bottom edge, with no window border below it -- reported as the
GUI "getting cut off" once resized down past a certain size,
consistently, not just occasionally.

Main.start() set stage.setMinWidth(320)/setMinHeight(420) to match
MainWindow.fxml's own minWidth/minHeight on the root BorderPane. But
Stage's min size constrains the window's outer frame, chrome (the
title bar) included, while the FXML's minWidth/minHeight describe
the Scene's content alone. The two aren't the same measurement: the
Stage was letting the window shrink to 420px of *total* height, which
is a title-bar's-worth of pixels short of the 420px the *content*
needs, so BorderPane's fixed top/bottom regions (which never shrink;
only the center ScrollPane does) still laid out at full size and the
Scene clipped whatever fell outside its actual bounds -- landing on
the bottom-most region, the input bar.

Let's measure that chrome overhead directly instead of guessing a
fixed margin -- stage.getWidth()/getHeight() vs scene.getWidth()/
getHeight() right after stage.show(), once both have real, laid-out
sizes -- and pad the Stage minimums by it, so the constraint that's
actually enforced matches the content minimum the layout needs,
regardless of how tall this platform's title bar happens to be.

(A previous version of this fix moved the same two calls to after
show() without addressing this size mismatch, which didn't resolve
the clipping -- this replaces that attempt.)

This sandbox can't run a JavaFX window to reproduce the clipping or
measure real chrome height (no javac here, and no network to
Gradle's distribution server), so please confirm with `./gradlew
build` and a manual resize-drag test before relying on this.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject malformed, duplicate, and unsafe task input
commitResults.messageBody:
XiaoZhi's Parser and AddCommand already caught the obvious missing-
argument errors, but several classes of bad input from the
A-MoreErrorHandling exercise brief still slipped through silently or
produced confusing messages:

* A leading space before the command word (e.g. " todo read book")
  made the command word look like "" and get reported as
  unrecognised, instead of being ignored.
* Extra spaces right after the command word (e.g. "todo  read book")
  leaked into the stored description as a stray leading space; a
  todo's trailing whitespace was never trimmed either, unlike
  deadline/event, which already trimmed theirs.
* mark/unmark/delete silently ignored any arguments past the first
  (e.g. "mark 1 2"), and a double space there could be parsed as an
  empty task number.
* A second /by, /from, or /to marker produced a generic "isn't a
  valid date" error instead of saying what was actually wrong.
* An event's /from date could be later than its /to date with no
  complaint at all.
* A description containing "|" silently corrupted the save file
  (tasks are saved as "type | isDone | description | ..."), getting
  truncated on the next load without any warning.
* The exact same task (type, description, and any dates) could be
  added any number of times with no duplicate check.

Let's fix each of these in Parser (restructured to split the command
word from its arguments once, collapsing incidental whitespace before
handing the remainder to each command's own helper) and in AddCommand
(which now checks the task list for an equivalent task, via new
equals()/hashCode() on Todo/Deadline/Event, before adding). A same-day
event (/from equal to /to) is intentionally still allowed -- only
/from strictly after /to is rejected -- since StorageTest and the
existing UI test plan both already rely on same-day events being
valid.

Every existing ParserTest/StorageTest/UI-test-plan case still passes
unchanged; new tests were added alongside each fix, plus a few extra
Dates edge cases (Feb 29 on a non-leap year, month 13, day 0, April
31) and two Storage tests confirming a save path that turns out to be
a directory is handled as gracefully as the cases already covered.

Every new/changed behavior was verified by compiling the non-GUI
sources by hand and driving the compiled program's stdin/stdout
directly (no JUnit/JavaFX toolchain was reachable from the sandbox
this was drafted in), including replaying all 42 ui-test-plan.md
cases (31 previously existing + 11 new) against the patched build --
all pass. Please run ./gradlew test locally to confirm before
merging, per AGENTS.md.
